rows.title: 1920 Memorial Cup — Grokipedia
matches: The 1920 Memorial Cup was the second edition of the Canadian junior ice hockey championship, contested as a two-game, total-goal series at Toronto's Arena Gardens between the Eastern champions, the Toronto Canoe Club Paddlers, and the Western champions, the Selkirk Fishermen. [1] The Paddlers dominated the series, winning 10–1 in Game 1 on March 23 and 5–4 in Game 2 on March 25, for a 15–5 aggregate victory and their first national title. [1] [2]

The Toronto Canoe Club earned the OHA junior title—and their path to the eastern final—by defeating the Stratford Midgets in a best-of-three, total-goal series. They lost the opening game 6–5 but rebounded with a decisive 10–2 victory in the second game, clinching the series on an aggregate score of 15–8. [4] As OHA champions, the Paddlers advanced to face Loyola College, the Quebec Amateur Hockey Association junior winners, in a single-game showdown for the George Richardson Trophy on March 19, 1920, at the Arena Gardens in Toronto, where they prevailed 16–4 to secure eastern supremacy. [4] [7]

In the west, the Selkirk Fishermen first captured the MJHL crown by winning the Turnbull Memorial Trophy as Manitoba junior champions, then advanced by defeating the Regina Victorias to claim the Manitoba-Saskatchewan regional title in early March 1920. They qualified for the Memorial Cup by winning the Abbott Cup as western Canada junior champions, overcoming the Alberta-British Columbia titlist Calgary Monarchs in a two-game total-goal series. Selkirk took the opener 8–2 before tying the second game 3–3, earning the series on a combined 11–5 scoreline. [2] [8]
In a tightly contested match, the Toronto Canoe Club Paddlers edged out the Selkirk Fishermen 5-4, clinching the total-goal series victory with an aggregate score of 15-5. [4] [11]

The 1920 Memorial Cup championship series between the Toronto Canoe Club Paddlers and the Selkirk Fishermen was a two-game, total-goals format contested at the Arena Gardens in Toronto, resulting in a decisive 15–5 aggregate victory for Toronto. Game 1 ended 10–1 in favor of the Paddlers on March 23, showcasing their offensive dominance with six goals in the third period alone, while Game 2 concluded 5–4 on March 25 in a closer but still controlled affair. This lopsided outcome highlighted Toronto's superior size, skill, and combination play against the plucky but outmatched Selkirk squad. [4]

Highlights of the series included Burch's sharp puck-carrying and net-front presence in Game 1, where Toronto's fast combinations overwhelmed Selkirk after an even second period, and the Fishermen's resilient rally in Game 2 that kept the contest competitive until the end. The series set no formal records in 1920, but Toronto's 10-goal margin in the opener stood as a testament to their pre-series form, having previously routed opponents like the Fort William Beavers 16–1. Burch's dominance foreshadowed his future NHL success, cementing his reputation as a junior hockey phenom. Following the series, Toronto defended their title in a challenge game against the Fort William Beavers, winning 11–1 on March 31. [4]

The Toronto Canoe Club Paddlers, as junior champions of the Ontario Hockey Association in 1920, fielded a young roster primarily composed of players under the age of 20, blending defensive solidity with potent forward scoring to secure the Memorial Cup. Coached by Dick Carroll, a veteran of professional hockey who guided the team through the playoffs, the lineup featured versatile athletes who contributed to a dominant 15-5 total-goal series victory over the Selkirk Fishermen. articleBody: 1919/20 SELKIRK FISHERMEN ABBOTT CUP TROPHY MANITOBA/SASKATCHEWAN CHAMPIONS TURNBULL MEMORIAL TROPHY The Selkirk Fishermen are the longest running junior hockey team in Canada. The franchise was founded in 1917, and joined the Winnipeg and District Junior League inaugural season in 1918. The league changed its name to the Manitoba Junior Hockey League in 1931. In its first year, the WDJL had nine teams in two divisions; each team played six games with the Fishermen taking the first league title in 1918. In 1920 the team won the league title again, claiming the new Turnbull Memorial Trophy. The team advanced to the Western Canada playdowns in Regina where they defeated the hometown Vics to claim the Manitoba/Saskatchewan title. Knocking off the Alberta/BC champion Calgary Monarchs earned Selkirk the Abbott Cup and the Junior hockey championship of Western Canada. This earned the Fishermen a crack at the Memorial Cup against the Eastern Champion, Toronto Canoe Club Paddlers. The popular Fishermen were small and success for them came from a fast, skilled offence. The Paddlers however, were an all-star contingent comprised of players from across the country and their size would prove to be too much for the Fishermen. Selkirk lost the two-game total goal Memorial Cup series 15-5. Roster; S. Thorsteinson, J. Heap, Johnny Shepard, G. Dalman, H.Brandow, C. Davies, W. Berrisford, S. Daly, F. Lockhart, H. Wolwin, R. Warwick, S.West (Trainer), A. Gilhooly (Trainer), S. Kennedy (Mgr), D. Saunders (Secretary), G. Gordon (Executive), J.Thorsteinson (Mascot)
